question.text: A body begins moving with an initial speed u and travels along a straight path. It covers the first half of the total distance with a constant acceleration a₁, and then covers the second half of the distance with a constant acceleration a₂. Demonstrate that its speed at the end of the journey is equal to the final speed it would attain if it traversed the entire path with a single uniform acceleration of (a₁ + a₂)/2.
conditions: first half of distance s traversed with constant acceleration a₁
second half of distance s traversed with constant acceleration a₂
compared with total distance 2s traversed with uniform acceleration (a₁ + a₂)/2

figure.description: A diagram comparing two cases of linear motion. Case 1 shows a particle starting with velocity u, traversing a displacement s under constant acceleration a₁ to reach velocity v₁, and then traversing an equal displacement s under constant acceleration a₂ to reach final velocity v₂. Case 2 shows the particle starting with velocity u, traversing the total displacement 2s under uniform acceleration (a₁ + a₂)/2, and attaining final velocity v.

solution.approach: Apply v² = u² + 2as across each half with a₁ and a₂, then compare the result with the same formula applied to the whole distance under the average acceleration.

steps.text: After the first half of distance s with acceleration a₁, the velocity v₁ satisfies this.
After the second half of distance s with acceleration a₂, starting from v₁, the velocity v₂ satisfies this.
For the whole distance 2s covered with the uniform acceleration (a₁ + a₂)/2 starting from u, the final velocity v satisfies this.
Both expressions for the squared final velocity are the same, so the final speeds are equal.
steps.why_this_step: Two non-negative quantities with equal squares must be equal.

final_answer.value: v₂ = v, so the final velocity covering the whole distance with uniform acceleration (a₁ + a₂)/2 equals the final velocity of the two-stage motion; proved as v₂² = v² = u² + 2s(a₁ + a₂).

common_mistakes.text: Applying v² = u² + 2 × (a₁ + a₂)/2 × s with distance s instead of full distance 2s gives u² + s(a₁ + a₂), which does not match v₂² and breaks the proof.
